import math

a = math.sqrt(3)
b = math.sqrt(2)
B = math.radians(45)

# Law of sines: sin A = a*sin B / b. Since a > b, both A and 180 - A are candidates.
s = a * math.sin(B) / b
A1 = math.asin(s)
A2 = math.pi - A1

solutions = []
for A in (A1, A2):
    C = math.pi - A - B
    if C <= 1e-12:
        print("REJECT: non-positive C for A =", round(math.degrees(A), 9))
        continue
    c = b * math.sin(C) / math.sin(B)
    # Verify with law of cosines for side b: b^2 = a^2 + c^2 - 2ac cos B
    residual = b * b - (a * a + c * c - 2 * a * c * math.cos(B))
    ok = abs(residual) < 1e-9
    solutions.append((math.degrees(A), math.degrees(C), c))
    print("A = %.6f deg, C = %.6f deg, c = %.12f, law-of-cosines residual = %.2e, %s"
          % (math.degrees(A), math.degrees(C), c, residual, "valid" if ok else "invalid"))

print("sin A (exact value sqrt(3)/2) numeric:", round(s, 12))
print("Number of valid triangles found:", len(solutions))

)

        for sA, sC, sc in [(sub_A, sub_C, sub_c)])
    for A, C, c in solutions
)

print("Submitted triple matches a valid solution:", matches_some)
print("Submitted answer covers all solutions:", covers_all)
if matches_some and covers_all:
    print("CHECK PASS")
else:
    print("CHECK FAIL: submitted answer omits the second solution A = 120 deg, C = 15 deg, c = sqrt(2 - sqrt(3))")
